metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Scores in win
metadata.description: Adkins caught all three of his targets for 32 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for six yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Adkins played 23 of the Broncos' 62 offensive snaps while also contributing six snaps to the special teams unit. The No. 3 tight end had a very reliable night, catching everything thrown his way and scoring a fourth-quarter touchdown to tie the game at 13 points.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Back in pads Monday
metadata.description: Adkins (undisclosed) participated during the Broncos' training camp practice Monday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Adkins left practice with a trainer Friday after presumably suffering some type of injury, but it looks like it wasn't anything too serious. He'll continue to compete with the likes of rookie fifth-rounder Justin Joly and Lucas Krull for a depth role at tight end during the upcoming campaign.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Doesn't practice Saturday
metadata.description: Adkins (undisclosed) did not participate in Saturday's training camp practice, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Adkins left Friday's practice with a trainer, but the nature and severity of the injury is not clear. He appeared in nine regular-season games for the Broncos last year, finishing with six catches (on 11 targets) for 48 yards and a touchdown. Adkins is competing against rookie fifth-rounder Justin Joly for the TE3 role behind Evan Engram and Adam Trautman.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins signs one-year deal to remain with Broncos
metadata.description: Nate Adkins and the Broncos have agreed on a one-year contract extension to keep the blocking tight end in Denver for another season.
metadata.analysis: Not long after re-signing Adam Trautman, the Broncos locked up another of their tight ends with Adkins signing a one-year extension. The tight end, who will be entering his fourth NFL season in 2026, caught six passes for 48 yards and a touchdown in nine games, while playing 33% of Denver's offensive snaps, last season. Known much more for his blocking, Adkins has just 24 career catches in 36 NFL games. He'll be off the fantasy radar in 2026.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Sticking around Denver
metadata.description: Adkins and the Broncos agreed on a one-year contract Sunday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Adkins will remain in Denver for a fourth season after operating having caught six of 11 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown over nine regular-season contests in 2025. The tight end will likely continue to have limited upside on offense next season, operating behind the likes of Evan Engram and Adam Trautman, the latter of which inked a three-year deal with the Broncos on Sunday.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Scores one touchdown in 2025
metadata.description: Adkins finished the 2025 regular-season campaign with six catches on 11 targets for 48 yards and one touchdown across nine appearances.
metadata.analysis: Adkins did not play a significant role for the Broncos this season, as the tight end missed time with ankle and knee injuries during the 2025 campaign. The 26-year-old operated as Denver's No. 3 tight end behind Evan Engram and Adam Trautman, so even when he was healthy, Adkins faced an uphill battle for playing time. The South Carolina product is set to become a restricted free agent this offseason, so the Broncos will have the opportunity to match any offers he may receiver from other teams to keep him in Denver. Regardless of where Adkins ends up playing in 2026, he'll likely continue to be far off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Adkins (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official website reports.
metadata.analysis: Adkins was able to log a full practice after opening the week as a limited participant Wednesday, moving past the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 17 win over the Chiefs. The tight end will likely operate in his traditional depth role behind Evan Engram and Adam Trautman in Sunday's matchup with the Chargers.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Limited in Wednesday's practice
metadata.description: Adkins (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Adkins was unable to play against the Chiefs on Christmas Day due to a knee injury, which also caused him to miss five games from Weeks 9 through 14. His ability to practice in a limited fashion indicates that he is progressing in his recovery, and he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers if he were to log a full practice over the next two days.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - Won't play vs. Kansas City
metadata.description: Adkins (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: A knee injury prevented Adkins from participating in any of the walkthrough practices during Week 17 prep, and he won't be on the Broncos' active roster for Christmas Day. Evan Engram and Adam Trautman are the only two tight ends on the active roster heading into Thursday's game. Adkins' next opportunity to play is Week 18 against the Chargers.

metadata.title: Nate Adkins - DNP in Tuesday walkthrough
metadata.description: Adkins (knee) did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Adkins has suited up in consecutive games after missing five due to a knee injury, which he potentially reaggravated last Sunday against the Jaguars. The tight end left in the first half and was unable to return to the game, a report that, combined with Tuesday's practice participation, does not bode well for his chances of playing in Thursday night's game against the Chiefs. Adkins will have one more chance to increase his participation level in the hopes of avoiding an injury designation ahead of Thursday's contest.
